records.content_title: India’s dengue burden: All 4 virus strains circulate together in several states, DENV 2 most widespread
records.content:
The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) has revealed that four dengue virus serotypes - 1,2,3,4 have been simultaneously circulating across India, a trend that may shape the country’s dengue preparedness strategies.

The study, conducted by the ICMR through its Virus Research and Diagnostic Laboratory (VRDL) network, analysed 6,889 laboratory-confirmed dengue samples collected from 45 laboratories across 25 States and Union Territories (UTs) between May 2023 and May 2025. DENV-2 was the most frequently reported serotype nationwide, accounting for 51 per cent of tested cases. It was followed by DENV-3 (13 per cent), DENV-1 (7 per cent) and DENV-4 (1 per cent).

Researchers found that every state and UT included in the study had at least two dengue serotypes circulating, indicating that dengue has become increasingly hyperendemic across India. According to the study, India contributes to 34 per cent (33 million) of the global burden of symptomatic dengue infections. Approximately 8.9 to 12.6 million primary infections are estimated to occur annually in the country among people aged 5 to 45.

.India gets its first Dengue vaccine—QDENGA.

“Molecular surveillance of dengue serotypes at regular intervals is critical for understanding serotype transmission dynamics and their burden on public health,” the authors wrote. They felt that earlier studies, although valuable, “were confined to smaller geographies” and “were not representative of temporal patterns.” Hence, could not be used for planning national strategies.

“The enhanced testing capabilities at the site laboratories also establish a robust platform for responding to future dengue epidemics, which pose a significant healthcare burden due to climate change, spread of vector mosquitoes and rapid urbanisation.”

Another concerning factor was patients facing concurrent infections. The study noted that such people were more likely to face thrombocytopenia (extremely low platelet count), hemorrhagic manifestations, and severe joint issues.

In most cases, dengue infection causes high fever, headache, weakness and muscle pain, but in severe cases it can be life-threatening. It can potentially lead to organ failure or severe bleeding if left untreated for a long time.

(CBS12) — Health officials issued a mosquito-borne illness advisory Monday after confirming a locally acquired case of dengue fever in Palm Beach County. The Florida Department of Health in Palm Beach County said it is working with Palm Beach County Mosquito Control to conduct surveillance and prevention efforts following the confirmed infection. A locally acquired case means the person was infected by a mosquito in the area rather than while traveling to a place where dengue is more common. Health officials did not release information about the patient or identify where in Palm Beach County the infection is believed to have occurred. Dengue is spread to people through the bite of an infected mosquito. The illness can cause fever, headache, pain behind the eyes, muscle and joint pain, nausea, vomiting and a rash. Some infections can develop into severe dengue, which may cause serious bleeding, shock or other potentially life-threatening complications. Virginia resident has state’s 1st locally acquired case of dengue fever Catherine Chen | catherine.chen@wtop.com August 5, 2026, 5:43 AM Share This: share on facebook share on X share on threads share on linkedin share on email print The Virginia Department of Health said the patient was sickened by the mosquito-borne virus but had not recently traveled outside the state. Virginia health officials have confirmed the state’s first known case of locally acquired dengue, a viral disease usually associated with international travel. The Virginia Department of Health said the person, who lives in Northern Virginia, became sick but had not recently traveled outside the state. Instead, the patient had been near another Virginia resident who was infected with dengue overseas. Health officials believe a local mosquito likely bit the traveler and later spread the virus to the second resident. Other health news DC region must prepare for disease-carrying mosquitos entering ‘prime-time season’ School backpack overload: Heavy bags can strain kids’ bodies Michigan reports the first 2 US deaths related to a diarrhea-causing parasite Officials said the risk to the public remains low, but the case is a reminder to protect yourself from mosquito bites during the summer months. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, dengue is spread by Aedes mosquitoes and is not passed directly from person to person. Symptoms can include fever, pain behind the eyes, muscle and joint pain, nausea and rash. Most people recover within a week, though some infections can become severe and require hospitalization. Health officials recommend using EPA-registered insect repellent and emptying standing water around homes where mosquitoes can breed. According to the Virginia Department of Health, the state’s mosquito season typically runs from early May through early November.
